And the messenger of the LORD called to Abraham from the sky a second time and said, “By myself I have sworn — this is the LORD's word — because you have done this and have not held back your son, your only one: I will bless you and bless you, and multiply and multiply your offspring, like the stars of the sky and like the sand on the shore of the sea. And your offspring will take possession of the gate of their enemies. And in your offspring all the nations of the earth will be blessed — because you listened to my voice.” And Abraham went back to his young men, and they got up and went together to Beersheba. And Abraham lived at Beersheba.

And after these things Abraham was told, “Milcah has borne children too, to your brother Nahor: Uz his firstborn, and Buz his brother, and Kemuel the father of Aram, and Chesed, and Hazo, and Pildash, and Jidlaph, and Bethuel.” And Bethuel fathered Rebekah. These eight Milcah bore to Nahor, Abraham's brother. And his concubine, whose name was Reumah, also bore Tebah, Gaham, Tahash, and Maacah.

chapters.label: Chapter 23
chapters.title: The Cave at Machpelah
paragraphs: And Sarah lived a hundred and twenty-seven years — these were the years of Sarah's life. And Sarah died at Kiriath-arba (that is, Hebron) in the land of Canaan, and Abraham came to mourn for Sarah and to weep for her. And Abraham got up from beside his dead and spoke to the Hittites: “I am a stranger and a settler among you. Give me a burial holding among you, so I can bury my dead out of my sight.” And the Hittites answered Abraham: “Hear us, my lord. You are a prince of God among us. Bury your dead in the choicest of our tombs. Not one of us will withhold his tomb from you, from burying your dead.”

And Abraham got up and bowed to the people of the land, the Hittites. And he spoke with them: “If it suits you that I should bury my dead out of my sight, then hear me and speak for me to Ephron son of Zohar, so he will give me the cave of Machpelah, which belongs to him, at the end of his field. Let him give it to me for the full price, as a burial holding among you.” Now Ephron was sitting among the Hittites, and Ephron the Hittite answered Abraham in the hearing of the Hittites, of everyone who came in at the gate of his city: “No, my lord, hear me. I give you the field, and I give you the cave that is in it. In the presence of my people I give it to you. Bury your dead.”

And Abraham bowed before the people of the land, and he spoke to Ephron in the hearing of the people of the land: “If only you would hear me — I am giving the price of the field. Take it from me, and let me bury my dead there.” And Ephron answered Abraham: “My lord, listen to me. Land worth four hundred shekels of silver — what is that between me and you? Bury your dead.” And Abraham listened to Ephron, and Abraham weighed out for Ephron the silver he had named in the hearing of the Hittites: four hundred shekels of silver, at the merchants' rate.

So Ephron's field at Machpelah, facing Mamre — the field and the cave in it and all the trees in the field, within all its borders — passed to Abraham as a possession, in the presence of the Hittites, before everyone who came in at the gate of his city. And after that Abraham buried Sarah his wife in the cave of the field of Machpelah, facing Mamre (that is, Hebron) in the land of Canaan. So the field and the cave in it passed to Abraham from the Hittites as a burial holding.

chapters.label: Chapter 24
chapters.title: Rebekah at the Well
paragraphs: And Abraham was old, well along in years, and the LORD had blessed Abraham in everything. And Abraham said to the senior servant of his household, the one in charge of everything he had, “Put your hand under my thigh. I want you to swear by the LORD, God of heaven and God of the earth, that you will not take a wife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanites I live among. You will go to my own country, to my own kindred, and take a wife for my son Isaac.” And the servant said to him, “Suppose the woman is not willing to follow me to this land. Should I take your son back to the land you came from?” And Abraham said to him, “Be careful not to take my son back there. The LORD, God of heaven, who took me from my father's house and from the land of my birth, who spoke to me and swore to me, ‘To your offspring I will give this land’ — he will send his messenger ahead of you, and you will take a wife for my son from there. And if the woman is not willing to follow you, you are released from this oath of mine. Only do not take my son back there.” And the servant put his hand under the thigh of Abraham his master and swore to him about this matter.

And the servant took ten of his master's camels and set out, with all kinds of good things from his master in his hand. And he got up and went to Aram-naharaim, to the city of Nahor. And he made the camels kneel outside the city by the well of water, toward evening, the time when the women come out to draw water. And he said, “LORD, God of my master Abraham, let it turn out well for me today, and show kindness to my master Abraham. Look — I am standing here by the spring of water, and the daughters of the men of the city are coming out to draw water. Let it be that the young woman I say to, ‘Please tip your jar so I can drink,’ and she says, ‘Drink — and I will water your camels too,’ let her be the one you have appointed for your servant Isaac. And by that I will know that you have shown kindness to my master.”

And before he had finished speaking — there was Rebekah coming out, who was born to Bethuel son of Milcah, the wife of Nahor, Abraham's brother, with her jar on her shoulder. And the young woman was very beautiful, a virgin; no man had known her. And she went down to the spring and filled her jar and came up. And the servant ran to meet her and said, “Please give me a little water from your jar.” And she said, “Drink, my lord.” And she hurried and lowered her jar onto her hand and gave him a drink. And when she had finished giving him a drink, she said, “I will draw for your camels too, until they have finished drinking.” And she hurried and emptied her jar into the trough and ran back to the well to draw, and she drew for all his camels. And the man was watching her in silence, waiting to know whether the LORD had made his journey succeed or not.

And when the camels had finished drinking, the man took a gold nose ring weighing half a shekel and two bracelets for her wrists weighing ten shekels of gold, and said, “Whose daughter are you? Tell me — is there room in your father's house for us to spend the night?” And she said to him, “I am the daughter of Bethuel, the son Milcah bore to Nahor.” And she said to him, “We have plenty of straw and feed, and room to spend the night.” And the man bowed his head and bowed down to the LORD, and said, “Blessed be the LORD, God of my master Abraham, who has not abandoned his kindness and his faithfulness toward my master. As for me, the LORD has led me on the road to the house of my master's kin.”

And the young woman ran and told her mother's household about these things. Now Rebekah had a brother named Laban, and Laban ran out to the man, to the spring. When he saw the nose ring, and the bracelets on his sister's wrists, and when he heard the words of Rebekah his sister — “This is what the man said to me” — he came out to the man, and there he was, standing with the camels at the spring. And he said, “Come in, blessed of the LORD. Why are you standing outside? I have cleared the house, and made room for the camels.” And the man came into the house, and Laban unloaded the camels and gave straw and feed to the camels and water to wash his feet and the feet of the men with him. And food was set in front of him, but he said, “I will not eat until I have said what I came to say.” And he said, “Speak.”

And he said, “I am Abraham's servant. And the LORD has blessed my master greatly, and he has become great. He has given him flocks and herds, silver and gold, male and female slaves, camels and donkeys. And Sarah, my master's wife, bore a son to my master in her old age, and he has given him everything he has. And my master made me swear: ‘You will not take a wife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanites in whose land I live. Instead you will go to my father's house, to my clan, and take a wife for my son.’ And I said to my master, ‘Suppose the woman will not follow me.’ And he said to me, ‘The LORD, in front of whom I have walked, will send his messenger with you and make your journey succeed, and you will take a wife for my son from my clan, from my father's house. Then you will be released from my oath — when you come to my clan. And if they will not give her to you, you are released from my oath.’

“And I came to the spring today, and I said, ‘LORD, God of my master Abraham, if you are going to make the journey I am on succeed — look, I am standing by the spring of water. Let it be that the young woman who comes out to draw, and I say to her, Please give me a little water from your jar to drink, and she says to me, You drink, and I will draw for your camels too — let her be the woman the LORD has appointed for my master's son.’ And before I had finished speaking in my heart — there was Rebekah coming out with her jar on her shoulder. And she went down to the spring and drew, and I said to her, ‘Please give me a drink.’ And she hurried and lowered her jar from her shoulder and said, ‘Drink — and I will water your camels too.’ So I drank, and she watered the camels too. And I asked her, ‘Whose daughter are you?’ And she said, ‘The daughter of Bethuel, Nahor's son, whom Milcah bore to him.’ And I put the ring on her nose and the bracelets on her wrists. And I bowed my head and bowed down to the LORD, and blessed the LORD, God of my master Abraham, who led me on the true road to take the daughter of my master's brother for his son. And now, if you are going to deal kindly and faithfully with my master, tell me. And if not, tell me, so I can turn to the right or to the left.”

And Laban and Bethuel answered, “This has come from the LORD. We cannot say anything to you, bad or good. Rebekah is in front of you. Take her and go, and let her be the wife of your master's son, as the LORD has spoken.” And when Abraham's servant heard their words, he bowed to the ground before the LORD. And the servant brought out objects of silver and objects of gold and clothing, and gave them to Rebekah, and he gave costly gifts to her brother and her mother. And he ate and drank, he and the men with him, and they spent the night.

And in the morning they got up, and he said, “Send me off to my master.” And her brother and her mother said, “Let the young woman stay with us a while, ten days or so. After that she can go.” And he said to them, “Don't hold me back, now that the LORD has made my journey succeed. Send me off, so I can go to my master.” And they said, “We will call the young woman and ask her.” And they called Rebekah and said to her, “Will you go with this man?” And she said, “I will go.” So they sent off Rebekah their sister, and her nurse, and Abraham's servant and his men. And they blessed Rebekah and said to her, “Our sister, may you become thousands upon thousands, and may your offspring take possession of the gate of those who hate them.” And Rebekah got up, with her young women, and they mounted the camels and followed the man. And the servant took Rebekah and went.

Now Isaac had come from the direction of Beer-lahai-roi; he was living in the Negev. And Isaac went out to walk in the field toward evening, and he looked up and saw — there were camels coming. And Rebekah looked up and saw Isaac, and she got down from the camel. And she said to the servant, “Who is that man walking in the field to meet us?” And the servant said, “That is my master.” So she took her veil and covered herself. And the servant told Isaac everything he had done. And Isaac brought her into the tent of Sarah his mother, and he took Rebekah, and she became his wife, and he loved her. And Isaac was comforted after his mother's death.

chapters.label: Chapter 25
chapters.title: Two Nations
paragraphs: And Abraham took another wife, whose name was Keturah. And she bore him Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah. And Jokshan fathered Sheba and Dedan, and the sons of Dedan were the Asshurim, the Letushim, and the Leummim. And the sons of Midian: Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, Abida, and Eldaah. All these were the descendants of Keturah. And Abraham gave everything he had to Isaac. But to the sons of his concubines Abraham gave gifts, and while he was still alive he sent them away from Isaac his son, eastward, to the land of the east.

And these are the days of the years of Abraham's life: a hundred and seventy-five years. And Abraham breathed his last and died at a good old age, an old man, full of years, and he was gathered to his people. And Isaac and Ishmael his sons buried him in the cave of Machpelah, in the field of Ephron son of Zohar the Hittite, facing Mamre — the field Abraham bought from the Hittites. There Abraham was buried, and Sarah his wife. And after Abraham's death, God blessed Isaac his son. And Isaac settled near Beer-lahai-roi.

And these are the generations of Ishmael, Abraham's son, whom Hagar the Egyptian, Sarah's slave, bore to Abraham. These are the names of Ishmael's sons, by their names, in the order of their birth: Nebaioth the firstborn of Ishmael, then Kedar, Adbeel, Mibsam, Mishma, Dumah, Massa, Hadad, Tema, Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah. These are Ishmael's sons, and these are their names, by their villages and their camps — twelve chieftains of their tribes. And these are the years of Ishmael's life: a hundred and thirty-seven years. And he breathed his last and died, and was gathered to his people. And they lived from Havilah to Shur, which faces Egypt, in the direction of Assyria. He settled at odds with all his kin.

And these are the generations of Isaac, Abraham's son: Abraham fathered Isaac. And Isaac was forty years old when he took Rebekah as his wife, the daughter of Bethuel the Aramean of Paddan-aram, the sister of Laban the Aramean. And Isaac pleaded with the LORD for his wife, because she was barren. And the LORD granted his plea, and Rebekah his wife conceived. And the children shoved each other inside her, and she said, “If it is like this, why am I?” And she went to ask the LORD. And the LORD said to her: “Two nations are in your womb, and two peoples will part from your body. One people will be stronger than the other, and the older will serve the younger.”

And when her days to give birth were completed — there were twins in her womb. And the first came out red, all of him like a hairy coat, and they named him Esau. And after that his brother came out, and his hand was gripping Esau's heel, and he was named Jacob. Isaac was sixty years old when she bore them. And the boys grew up, and Esau was a man who knew hunting, a man of the open country; and Jacob was a quiet man, staying among the tents. And Isaac loved Esau, because he had a taste for wild game; but Rebekah loved Jacob.

And Jacob was boiling a stew, and Esau came in from the open country, and he was exhausted. And Esau said to Jacob, “Let me gulp down some of that red stuff — that red stuff — because I am exhausted.” That is why he was named Edom. And Jacob said, “Sell me your birthright today.” And Esau said, “Look, I am about to die. What good is a birthright to me?” And Jacob said, “Swear to me today.” And he swore to him, and he sold his birthright to Jacob. And Jacob gave Esau bread and lentil stew, and he ate and drank and got up and went off. So Esau despised his birthright.

chapters.label: Chapter 26
chapters.title: Isaac Digs the Wells Again
paragraphs: And there was a famine in the land, besides the first famine that happened in Abraham's time, and Isaac went to Abimelech king of the Philistines, at Gerar. And the LORD appeared to him and said, “Do not go down to Egypt. Live in the land I tell you. Stay in this land as a stranger, and I will be with you and bless you — because to you and to your offspring I will give all these lands, and I will keep the oath I swore to Abraham your father. And I will multiply your offspring like the stars of the sky, and I will give your offspring all these lands, and in your offspring all the nations of the earth will be blessed — because Abraham listened to my voice and kept my charge, my commands, my statutes, and my instructions.”

So Isaac settled in Gerar. And the men of the place asked about his wife, and he said, “She is my sister,” because he was afraid to say “my wife” — thinking, the men of the place might kill me over Rebekah, because she is beautiful. And when he had been there a long time, Abimelech king of the Philistines looked down through a window and saw — there was Isaac, playing with Rebekah his wife. And Abimelech called Isaac and said, “So she really is your wife! How could you say, ‘She is my sister’?” And Isaac said to him, “Because I thought I might die over her.” And Abimelech said, “What is this you have done to us? One of the people might easily have lain with your wife, and you would have brought guilt on us.” And Abimelech ordered all the people: “Whoever touches this man or his wife will certainly be put to death.”

And Isaac sowed in that land and reaped a hundredfold that same year, and the LORD blessed him. And the man became great, and he kept getting greater until he was very great. He had holdings of flocks and holdings of herds and a large household, and the Philistines envied him. And all the wells his father's servants had dug in the days of Abraham his father, the Philistines had stopped up and filled with dirt. And Abimelech said to Isaac, “Go away from us. You have become far too powerful for us.” So Isaac left there and camped in the Valley of Gerar and settled there.

And Isaac dug again the wells of water they had dug in the days of Abraham his father, which the Philistines had stopped up after Abraham's death, and he gave them the same names his father had given them. And Isaac's servants dug in the valley and found there a well of fresh water. And the herders of Gerar quarreled with Isaac's herders: “The water is ours.” So he named the well Esek, because they fought with him over it. And they dug another well, and they quarreled over that one too, and he named it Sitnah. And he moved on from there and dug another well, and over that one they did not quarrel, and he named it Rehoboth, and said, “Now the LORD has made room for us, and we will be fruitful in the land.”

And he went up from there to Beersheba. And the LORD appeared to him that night and said, “I am the God of Abraham your father. Do not be afraid, because I am with you. I will bless you and multiply your offspring, for the sake of Abraham my servant.” And he built an altar there and called on the name of the LORD, and pitched his tent there, and Isaac's servants dug a well there.

And Abimelech came to him from Gerar, with Ahuzzath his adviser and Phicol the commander of his army. And Isaac said to them, “Why have you come to me, when you hate me and sent me away from you?” And they said, “We have seen clearly that the LORD is with you, and we said, let there be an oath between us — between us and you — and let us cut a covenant with you: that you will do us no harm, just as we did not touch you, and did nothing but good for you, and sent you away in peace. You are now the blessed of the LORD.” And he made them a feast, and they ate and drank. And they got up early in the morning and swore to each other, and Isaac sent them off, and they left him in peace. And that same day Isaac's servants came and told him about the well they had dug, and said to him, “We have found water.” And he named it Shibah. That is why the name of the city is Beersheba to this day.
And Esau was forty years old when he took as wives Judith daughter of Beeri the Hittite and Basemath daughter of Elon the Hittite. And they were a bitterness of spirit to Isaac and Rebekah.

chapters.label: Chapter 27
chapters.title: The Stolen Blessing
paragraphs: When Isaac was old and his eyes had grown too dim to see, he called Esau his older son and said to him, “My son.” And he said, “Here I am.” And he said, “Look — I am old. I don't know the day of my death. So now take your gear, your quiver and your bow, and go out to the open country and hunt me some game. And make me the tasty food I love, and bring it to me so I can eat — so that I can bless you before I die.” And Rebekah was listening while Isaac spoke to Esau his son. And Esau went out to the open country to hunt game and bring it back.

And Rebekah said to Jacob her son, “Listen — I heard your father speaking to Esau your brother. He said, ‘Bring me game and make me tasty food, so I can eat and bless you in front of the LORD before my death.’ So now, my son, listen to my voice, to what I am telling you. Go to the flock and get me two good young goats from there, and I will make them into tasty food for your father, the kind he loves. And you will bring it to your father, so he can eat — so that he can bless you before his death.” And Jacob said to Rebekah his mother, “But Esau my brother is a hairy man, and I am a smooth man. Suppose my father touches me. I will look like a fraud to him, and I will bring a curse on myself and not a blessing.” And his mother said to him, “Your curse be on me, my son. Just listen to my voice. Go, get them for me.”

So he went and got them and brought them to his mother, and his mother made tasty food, the kind his father loved. And Rebekah took the best clothes of Esau her older son, which she had in the house, and put them on Jacob her younger son. And she put the skins of the young goats on his hands and on the smooth part of his neck. And she put the tasty food and the bread she had made into the hand of Jacob her son.

And he came to his father and said, “My father.” And he said, “Here I am. Who are you, my son?” And Jacob said to his father, “I am Esau, your firstborn. I have done what you told me. Get up, please, sit and eat from my game, so that you can bless me.” And Isaac said to his son, “How did you find it so quickly, my son?” And he said, “Because the LORD your God brought it to me.” And Isaac said to Jacob, “Come closer, so I can touch you, my son — whether you really are my son Esau or not.” And Jacob came close to Isaac his father, and he touched him and said, “The voice is Jacob's voice, but the hands are Esau's hands.” And he did not recognize him, because his hands were hairy like the hands of Esau his brother. So he blessed him. And he said, “Are you really my son Esau?” And he said, “I am.”

And he said, “Bring it close to me, and let me eat from my son's game, so that I can bless you.” And he brought it close to him, and he ate; and he brought him wine, and he drank. And Isaac his father said to him, “Come close and kiss me, my son.” And he came close and kissed him. And he smelled the smell of his clothes, and he blessed him and said: “See — the smell of my son is like the smell of a field the LORD has blessed. May God give you the dew of the sky, and the richness of the earth, and plenty of grain and new wine. May peoples serve you, and nations bow down to you. Be master over your brothers, and let your mother's sons bow down to you. Cursed be everyone who curses you, and blessed be everyone who blesses you.”

And it happened, as soon as Isaac had finished blessing Jacob — Jacob had barely gone out from the presence of Isaac his father — that Esau his brother came in from his hunting. And he too made tasty food and brought it to his father, and he said to his father, “Let my father get up and eat from his son's game, so that you can bless me.” And Isaac his father said to him, “Who are you?” And he said, “I am your son, your firstborn, Esau.” And Isaac shook with a very great trembling and said, “Then who was it that hunted game and brought it to me, and I ate it all before you came, and I blessed him? And blessed he will stay.”

When Esau heard his father's words, he cried out a great and very bitter cry, and said to his father, “Bless me too, my father!” And he said, “Your brother came with deceit, and he took your blessing.” And he said, “Is he not rightly named Jacob? He has cheated me these two times: he took my birthright, and look — now he has taken my blessing.” And he said, “Haven't you kept back a blessing for me?” And Isaac answered Esau, “Look — I have made him master over you, and I have given him all his brothers as servants, and I have sustained him with grain and new wine. So what can I do for you, my son?” And Esau said to his father, “Do you have only one blessing, my father? Bless me too, my father!” And Esau lifted up his voice and wept.

And Isaac his father answered him: “Look — away from the richness of the earth your home will be, and away from the dew of the sky above. And by your sword you will live, and you will serve your brother. But when you break loose, you will tear his yoke off your neck.” And Esau held a grudge against Jacob because of the blessing his father had given him, and Esau said in his heart, “The days of mourning for my father are coming close. Then I will kill Jacob my brother.”

And Rebekah was told the words of Esau her older son, and she sent and called Jacob her younger son and said to him, “Listen — Esau your brother is consoling himself about you by planning to kill you. So now, my son, listen to my voice. Get up, run to Laban my brother, in Haran, and stay with him a while, until your brother's fury dies down — until your brother's anger turns away from you and he forgets what you did to him. Then I will send and bring you back from there. Why should I lose both of you in one day?” And Rebekah said to Isaac, “I am sick of my life because of these Hittite women. If Jacob takes a wife from the Hittite women, from the women of this land, what good is my life to me?”

chapters.label: Chapter 28
chapters.title: The Ladder at Bethel
paragraphs: And Isaac called Jacob and blessed him, and gave him this charge: “Do not take a wife from the Canaanite women. Get up, go to Paddan-aram, to the house of Bethuel your mother's father, and take a wife from there, from the daughters of Laban your mother's brother. And may El Shaddai bless you and make you fruitful and multiply you, so that you become a company of peoples. And may he give you the blessing of Abraham — to you and to your offspring with you — so that you take possession of the land where you have lived as a stranger, which God gave to Abraham.” And Isaac sent Jacob off, and he went to Paddan-aram, to Laban son of Bethuel the Aramean, the brother of Rebekah, the mother of Jacob and Esau.

And Esau saw that Isaac had blessed Jacob and sent him off to Paddan-aram to take a wife there, and that when he blessed him he had charged him, “Do not take a wife from the Canaanite women,” and that Jacob had listened to his father and his mother and gone to Paddan-aram. And Esau saw that the Canaanite women were bad in the eyes of Isaac his father. So Esau went to Ishmael and took Mahalath daughter of Ishmael son of Abraham, the sister of Nebaioth, as a wife, in addition to the wives he had.

And Jacob went out from Beersheba and set out for Haran. And he came upon a certain place and stopped there for the night, because the sun had set. And he took one of the stones of that place and put it under his head, and lay down in that place. And he dreamed — and there was a stairway set on the earth with its top reaching the sky, and there were messengers of God going up and coming down on it. And there was the LORD, standing over him, and he said, “I am the LORD, the God of Abraham your father and the God of Isaac. The land you are lying on I will give to you and to your offspring. And your offspring will be like the dust of the earth, and you will spread out to the west and the east and the north and the south. And in you and in your offspring all the families of the earth will be blessed. And look — I am with you, and I will keep you wherever you go, and I will bring you back to this land. I will not leave you until I have done what I have promised you.”

And Jacob woke from his sleep and said, “Surely the LORD is in this place — and I did not know it.” And he was afraid, and he said, “How terrifying this place is. This is nothing but the house of God, and this is the gate of heaven.” And Jacob got up early in the morning and took the stone he had put under his head and set it up as a standing stone, and poured oil on the top of it. And he named that place Bethel — though the name of the city had been Luz before.

And Jacob made a vow: “If God will be with me and keep me on this road I am going, and give me bread to eat and clothes to wear, and I come back to my father's house in peace — then the LORD will be my God. And this stone I have set up as a standing stone will be God's house. And of everything you give me, I will give a tenth of it back to you.”

chapters.label: Chapter 29
chapters.title: Jacob Meets His Match
paragraphs: Then Jacob picked up his feet and went to the land of the people of the east. And he looked, and there was a well in the open country, and three flocks of sheep lying beside it, because the flocks were watered from that well. And the stone over the mouth of the well was large. When all the flocks were gathered there, the shepherds would roll the stone off the mouth of the well and water the sheep, and put the stone back in its place over the mouth of the well. And Jacob said to them, “My brothers, where are you from?” And they said, “We are from Haran.” And he said to them, “Do you know Laban son of Nahor?” And they said, “We know him.” And he said to them, “Is it well with him?” And they said, “It is well — and here is Rachel his daughter coming with the sheep.” And he said, “Look, the day is still high. It isn't time to gather the livestock. Water the sheep and go, graze them.” And they said, “We can't, until all the flocks are gathered and they roll the stone off the mouth of the well. Then we water the sheep.”

While he was still speaking with them, Rachel came with her father's sheep — she was a shepherd. And when Jacob saw Rachel the daughter of Laban his mother's brother, and the sheep of Laban his mother's brother, Jacob went up and rolled the stone off the mouth of the well and watered the flock of Laban his mother's brother. And Jacob kissed Rachel, and he lifted up his voice and wept. And Jacob told Rachel that he was her father's kinsman, that he was Rebekah's son, and she ran and told her father. And when Laban heard the news about Jacob his sister's son, he ran to meet him and threw his arms around him and kissed him and brought him to his house. And he told Laban all these things. And Laban said to him, “Truly you are my bone and my flesh.” And he stayed with him a full month.

And Laban said to Jacob, “Just because you are my kinsman, should you work for me for nothing? Tell me — what should your wages be?” Now Laban had two daughters. The name of the older was Leah, and the name of the younger was Rachel. And Leah's eyes were soft, but Rachel was shapely and beautiful. And Jacob loved Rachel, and he said, “I will work seven years for you for Rachel, your younger daughter.” And Laban said, “Better that I give her to you than that I give her to another man. Stay with me.” So Jacob worked seven years for Rachel, and they were like a few days in his eyes, because of his love for her.

And Jacob said to Laban, “Give me my wife. My time is finished, and I want to go in to her.” And Laban gathered all the men of the place and made a feast. And in the evening he took Leah his daughter and brought her to him, and he went in to her. And Laban gave Zilpah his slave to his daughter Leah as her slave. And in the morning — there was Leah. And he said to Laban, “What is this you have done to me? Wasn't it for Rachel that I worked for you? Why have you deceived me?” And Laban said, “It is not done that way in our place, to give the younger before the firstborn. Finish out this bridal week, and we will give you the other one too, for the work you will do for me another seven years.”

And Jacob did so, and finished out her week, and Laban gave him Rachel his daughter as a wife. And Laban gave Bilhah his slave to his daughter Rachel as her slave. And he went in to Rachel too, and he loved Rachel more than Leah. And he worked for Laban another seven years.

And the LORD saw that Leah was unloved, and he opened her womb; but Rachel was barren. And Leah conceived and bore a son, and she named him Reuben — because she said, “The LORD has seen my suffering. Now my husband will love me.” And she conceived again and bore a son, and she said, “Because the LORD heard that I am unloved, he has given me this one too.” And she named him Simeon. And she conceived again and bore a son, and she said, “Now, this time, my husband will be joined to me, because I have borne him three sons.” That is why he was named Levi. And she conceived again and bore a son, and she said, “This time I will praise the LORD.” That is why she named him Judah. And she stopped bearing.

chapters.label: Chapter 30
chapters.title: The Sisters, and the Flocks
paragraphs: And when Rachel saw that she was bearing Jacob no children, Rachel envied her sister. And she said to Jacob, “Give me children, or I am a dead woman.” And Jacob's anger flared against Rachel, and he said, “Am I in God's place? He is the one who has held back the fruit of your womb.” And she said, “Here is my slave Bilhah. Go in to her, and let her give birth on my knees, so that I too may be built up through her.” So she gave him Bilhah her slave as a wife, and Jacob went in to her. And Bilhah conceived and bore Jacob a son. And Rachel said, “God has judged my case, and he has also heard my voice and given me a son.” That is why she named him Dan. And Bilhah, Rachel's slave, conceived again and bore Jacob a second son. And Rachel said, “With mighty wrestlings I have wrestled with my sister, and I have won.” And she named him Naphtali.

When Leah saw that she had stopped bearing, she took Zilpah her slave and gave her to Jacob as a wife. And Zilpah, Leah's slave, bore Jacob a son. And Leah said, “What luck!” And she named him Gad. And Zilpah, Leah's slave, bore Jacob a second son. And Leah said, “How happy I am — women will call me happy.” And she named him Asher.

And in the days of the wheat harvest Reuben went out and found mandrakes in the field, and he brought them to Leah his mother. And Rachel said to Leah, “Please give me some of your son's mandrakes.” And she said to her, “Is it a small thing that you took my husband? Now you want to take my son's mandrakes too?” And Rachel said, “All right — he can lie with you tonight, in exchange for your son's mandrakes.” And Jacob came in from the field in the evening, and Leah went out to meet him and said, “You are coming in to me. I have hired you, fair and square, with my son's mandrakes.” And he lay with her that night. And God listened to Leah, and she conceived and bore Jacob a fifth son. And Leah said, “God has given me my wages, because I gave my slave to my husband.” And she named him Issachar. And Leah conceived again and bore Jacob a sixth son. And Leah said, “God has given me a good gift. This time my husband will honor me, because I have borne him six sons.” And she named him Zebulun. And afterward she bore a daughter and named her Dinah.

And God remembered Rachel, and God listened to her and opened her womb. And she conceived and bore a son, and she said, “God has taken away my disgrace.” And she named him Joseph, saying, “May the LORD add me another son.”

And when Rachel had borne Joseph, Jacob said to Laban, “Send me off, so I can go to my own place, to my own land. Give me my wives and my children, the ones I worked for, and let me go. You know the work I have done for you.” And Laban said to him, “If I have found favor in your eyes — I have learned by divination that the LORD has blessed me because of you.” And he said, “Name your wages, and I will pay them.” And he said to him, “You know how I have worked for you, and what has become of your livestock with me. What you had before I came was little, and it has burst out into a multitude, and the LORD has blessed you wherever I turned. And now, when do I get to provide for my own household?”

And he said, “What should I give you?” And Jacob said, “Don't give me anything. If you will do this one thing for me, I will go back to pasturing your flock and keeping it. Let me go through your whole flock today and take out of it every speckled and spotted animal, and every dark-colored one among the lambs, and the spotted and speckled among the goats. Those will be my wages. And my honesty will testify for me later, when you come to look over my wages: anything with me that is not speckled or spotted among the goats, or dark among the lambs, will count as stolen.” And Laban said, “Good — let it be as you say.” And that same day he took out the male goats that were streaked and spotted, and all the female goats that were speckled and spotted, every one with white on it, and all the dark ones among the lambs, and he put them in the hands of his sons. And he set three days' journey between himself and Jacob, while Jacob pastured the rest of Laban's flock.

And Jacob took fresh rods of poplar and almond and plane tree, and peeled white streaks in them, laying bare the white on the rods. And he set the rods he had peeled in front of the flocks, in the troughs, in the watering channels where the flocks came to drink — and they went into heat when they came to drink. And the flocks bred in front of the rods, and they bore young that were streaked, speckled, and spotted. And Jacob separated the lambs, and he turned the faces of the flock toward the streaked and all the dark ones in Laban's flock. And he put his own droves by themselves and did not put them with Laban's flock. And whenever the sturdy animals were breeding, Jacob would set the rods in the troughs in front of their eyes, so they would breed among the rods. But when the animals were weak he did not set them there — so the weak ones went to Laban and the sturdy ones to Jacob. And the man burst out and out: he had large flocks, and female and male slaves, and camels and donkeys.

chapters.label: Chapter 31
chapters.title: The Flight, and the Heap of Witness
paragraphs: And he heard the words of Laban's sons: “Jacob has taken everything that was our father's, and out of what belonged to our father he has built all this wealth.” And Jacob looked at Laban's face — and it was not toward him as it had been before. And the LORD said to Jacob, “Go back to the land of your fathers, to your kindred, and I will be with you.” And Jacob sent and called Rachel and Leah out to the field, to his flock, and said to them, “I see your father's face, that it is not toward me as it was before. But the God of my father has been with me. And you know that I have worked for your father with all my strength, and your father has cheated me and changed my wages ten times over — but God did not let him do me harm. If he said, ‘The speckled will be your wages,’ then the whole flock bore speckled; and if he said, ‘The streaked will be your wages,’ then the whole flock bore streaked. So God has taken away your father's livestock and given it to me.

“And at the time the flock was breeding, I looked up and saw in a dream — and there were the males mounting the flock, streaked and speckled and mottled. And the messenger of God said to me in the dream, ‘Jacob.’ And I said, ‘Here I am.’ And he said, ‘Look up and see: all the males mounting the flock are streaked and speckled and mottled, because I have seen everything Laban is doing to you. I am the God of Bethel, where you anointed a standing stone, where you made a vow to me. Now get up, go out of this land, and go back to the land of your birth.’” And Rachel and Leah answered him, “Is there any share or inheritance left for us in our father's house? Doesn't he treat us as foreigners? He sold us, and he has been eating up the money paid for us. All the wealth God has taken from our father belongs to us and to our children. So now — whatever God has told you, do it.”

Then Jacob got up and put his children and his wives on the camels. And he drove off all his livestock and all the property he had gathered, the livestock he had come to own in Paddan-aram, to go to Isaac his father in the land of Canaan. Now Laban had gone to shear his sheep, and Rachel stole the household gods that belonged to her father. And Jacob stole the heart of Laban the Aramean by not telling him he was running. So he ran, he and everything he had. He got up and crossed the river and set his face toward the hill country of Gilead.

And on the third day Laban was told that Jacob had run. And he took his kinsmen with him and chased after him seven days' journey, and caught up with him in the hill country of Gilead. And God came to Laban the Aramean in a dream at night and said to him, “Be careful you say nothing to Jacob, good or bad.” And Laban caught up with Jacob. Now Jacob had pitched his tent in the hill country, and Laban pitched with his kinsmen in the hill country of Gilead. And Laban said to Jacob, “What have you done, stealing my heart and driving my daughters off like prisoners of war? Why did you run in secret and steal away from me, and not tell me? I would have sent you off with joy and songs, with tambourine and lyre. And you didn't even let me kiss my grandchildren and my daughters goodbye. You have done a stupid thing. I have it in my hand to do you harm — but the God of your father spoke to me last night and said, ‘Be careful you say nothing to Jacob, good or bad.’ And now you have gone off because you were homesick for your father's house — but why did you steal my gods?”

And Jacob answered Laban, “Because I was afraid. I thought you would tear your daughters away from me. Whoever you find your gods with will not live. In front of our kinsmen, identify what is yours among my things and take it.” Now Jacob did not know that Rachel had stolen them. And Laban went into Jacob's tent, and into Leah's tent, and into the tents of the two slave women, and he did not find them. And he came out of Leah's tent and went into Rachel's tent. Now Rachel had taken the household gods and put them in the camel's saddle cushion and was sitting on them. And Laban felt all around the tent and did not find them. And she said to her father, “Don't let my lord be angry that I cannot get up in front of you — the way of women is on me.” So he searched and did not find the household gods.

And Jacob was furious, and he argued it out with Laban. Jacob answered Laban, “What is my offense? What is my sin, that you have come after me in hot pursuit? You have felt through all my things — what have you found of all your household goods? Set it here, in front of my kinsmen and yours, and let them decide between the two of us. Twenty years I have been with you. Your ewes and your she-goats never miscarried, and I never ate the rams of your flock. What was torn by animals I never brought to you — I bore the loss myself. You demanded it from my hand, whether it was stolen by day or stolen by night. This is how I was: by day the heat ate me, and the cold by night, and sleep fled from my eyes. Twenty years I have been in your house. I worked for you fourteen years for your two daughters, and six years for your flock, and you changed my wages ten times over. If the God of my father, the God of Abraham and the Terror of Isaac, had not been with me, you would have sent me away empty-handed now. God has seen my misery and the labor of my hands, and last night he handed down his verdict.”

And Laban answered Jacob, “The daughters are my daughters, the children are my children, the flocks are my flocks — everything you see is mine. And what can I do today about these daughters of mine, or about the children they have borne? So now — come, let us cut a covenant, you and I, and let it be a witness between me and you.” And Jacob took a stone and set it up as a standing stone. And Jacob said to his kinsmen, “Gather stones.” And they took stones and made a heap, and they ate there by the heap. And Laban called it Jegar-sahadutha, and Jacob called it Galeed. And Laban said, “This heap is a witness between me and you today.” That is why it was named Galeed — and Mizpah, because he said, “May the LORD keep watch between me and you when we are out of each other's sight.

“If you mistreat my daughters, or if you take other wives besides my daughters — no one is with us, but see: God is witness between me and you.” And Laban said to Jacob, “Here is this heap, and here is the standing stone I have set between me and you. This heap is a witness and the standing stone is a witness: I will not go past this heap to you, and you will not go past this heap and this standing stone to me, to do harm. May the God of Abraham and the God of Nahor — the God of their father — judge between us.” And Jacob swore by the Terror of his father Isaac. And Jacob offered a sacrifice in the hill country and called his kinsmen to eat bread, and they ate bread and spent the night in the hill country. And Laban got up early in the morning and kissed his grandchildren and his daughters and blessed them, and Laban went off and returned to his place.

chapters.label: Chapter 32
chapters.title: The Night at the Jabbok
paragraphs: And Jacob went on his way, and messengers of God met him. And when Jacob saw them he said, “This is God's camp.” And he named that place Mahanaim. And Jacob sent messengers ahead of him to Esau his brother, to the land of Seir, the country of Edom. And he ordered them: “Say this to my lord Esau — this is what your servant Jacob says: I have been living with Laban as a stranger, and I stayed until now. And I have oxen and donkeys, flocks and male and female slaves. And I have sent to tell my lord, so I may find favor in your eyes.” And the messengers came back to Jacob and said, “We went to your brother Esau, and he is coming to meet you — and four hundred men with him.”

And Jacob was very afraid, and it pressed in on him. And he split the people who were with him, and the flocks and the herds and the camels, into two camps. And he said, “If Esau comes to the one camp and strikes it, the camp that is left will get away.” And Jacob said, “God of my father Abraham, God of my father Isaac — the LORD who said to me, ‘Go back to your country and your kindred and I will do you good’ — I am too small for all the kindnesses and all the faithfulness you have shown your servant. With only my staff I crossed this Jordan, and now I have become two camps. Save me, please, from the hand of my brother, from the hand of Esau, because I am afraid of him — that he will come and strike me down, mothers with their children. And you said, ‘I will certainly do you good, and make your offspring like the sand of the sea, too many to be counted.’”

And he spent that night there, and out of what he had with him he took a gift for Esau his brother: two hundred female goats and twenty males, two hundred ewes and twenty rams, thirty nursing camels with their young, forty cows and ten bulls, twenty female donkeys and ten males. And he put them in the hands of his servants, each drove by itself, and said to his servants, “Cross over ahead of me, and leave a space between one drove and the next.” And he ordered the first one: “When Esau my brother meets you and asks you, ‘Whose man are you? Where are you going? Whose are these ahead of you?’ — then you say, ‘They belong to your servant Jacob. It is a gift, sent to my lord Esau. And look, he is behind us.’” And he ordered the second and the third and everyone following the droves the same way: “This is what you are to say to Esau when you find him. And say: ‘Look, your servant Jacob is behind us.’” Because he said to himself, “I will cover his face with the gift going ahead of me, and after that I will see his face. Maybe he will lift up my face.” So the gift crossed over ahead of him, and he spent that night in the camp.

And he got up that night and took his two wives and his two slave women and his eleven children and crossed the ford of the Jabbok. He took them and sent them across the stream, and he sent across everything he had. And Jacob was left alone. And a man wrestled with him until the breaking of day. And when he saw that he could not beat him, he struck the socket of his hip, and Jacob's hip was wrenched as he wrestled with him. And he said, “Let me go, because the day is breaking.” And he said, “I will not let you go unless you bless me.”

And he said to him, “What is your name?” And he said, “Jacob.” And he said, “Your name will no longer be Jacob but Israel — because you have wrestled with God and with men, and you have won.” And Jacob asked and said, “Tell me your name.” And he said, “Why is it you ask my name?” And he blessed him there.

And Jacob named the place Peniel — “because I have seen God face to face, and my life was spared.” And the sun rose on him as he passed Penuel, and he was limping because of his hip. That is why to this day the Israelites do not eat the thigh muscle that is on the socket of the hip: because he struck the socket of Jacob's hip at the thigh muscle.

chapters.label: Chapter 33
chapters.title: The Face of a Brother
paragraphs: And Jacob looked up and saw — there was Esau coming, and four hundred men with him. And he divided the children between Leah and Rachel and the two slave women. And he put the slave women and their children first, and Leah and her children after them, and Rachel and Joseph last. And he himself crossed over ahead of them, and he bowed to the ground seven times, until he came near his brother. And Esau ran to meet him and threw his arms around him and fell on his neck and kissed him. And they wept.

And he looked up and saw the women and the children, and said, “Who are these with you?” And he said, “The children God has graciously given your servant.” And the slave women came near, they and their children, and they bowed. And Leah too came near with her children, and they bowed. And afterward Joseph came near, and Rachel, and they bowed.

And he said, “What did you mean by this whole camp I met?” And he said, “To find favor in the eyes of my lord.” And Esau said, “I have plenty, my brother. Keep what is yours.” And Jacob said, “No — please, if I have found favor in your eyes, take my gift from my hand. For seeing your face is like seeing the face of God, and you have received me kindly. Please take my blessing that has been brought to you, because God has been gracious to me, and because I have everything.” And he pressed him, and he took it.

And he said, “Let's move on and go, and I will go alongside you.” And he said to him, “My lord knows that the children are frail, and the flocks and herds that are nursing are with me. If they are driven hard for a single day, all the flocks will die. Let my lord go on ahead of his servant, and I will move along slowly, at the pace of the livestock in front of me and the pace of the children, until I come to my lord at Seir.” And Esau said, “Then let me leave some of the people who are with me with you.” And he said, “Why do that? Let me find favor in the eyes of my lord.” So Esau turned back that day on his way to Seir.

And Jacob traveled to Succoth and built himself a house and made shelters for his livestock. That is why the place is named Succoth. And Jacob came safely to the city of Shechem, in the land of Canaan, when he came from Paddan-aram, and he camped in front of the city. And he bought the piece of land where he had pitched his tent from the sons of Hamor, Shechem's father, for a hundred pieces of silver. And he set up an altar there and called it El-elohe-Israel.

chapters.label: Chapter 34
chapters.title: Dinah
paragraphs: And Dinah, the daughter Leah had borne to Jacob, went out to see the women of the land. And Shechem son of Hamor the Hivite, the chief of the region, saw her, and he took her and lay with her and violated her. And he was bound to Dinah, Jacob's daughter, and he loved the girl, and he spoke to the girl's heart. And Shechem said to Hamor his father, “Get me this girl as a wife.” And Jacob heard that he had defiled Dinah his daughter — and his sons were with his livestock in the field, and Jacob said nothing until they came in. And Hamor, Shechem's father, went out to Jacob to speak with him. And Jacob's sons came in from the field when they heard, and the men were sickened, and they burned with anger, because he had done an outrage in Israel by lying with Jacob's daughter — a thing that should not be done.

And Hamor spoke with them: “My son Shechem is set on your daughter. Please give her to him as a wife. And make marriages with us: give us your daughters, and take our daughters for yourselves. And live with us. The land is open in front of you — settle in it, trade in it, get holdings in it.” And Shechem said to her father and her brothers, “Let me find favor in your eyes, and whatever you tell me, I will give. Ask me for as high a bride-price and gift as you like, and I will give whatever you tell me. Only give me the girl as a wife.”

And Jacob's sons answered Shechem and Hamor his father with deceit — because he had defiled Dinah their sister. And they said to them, “We can't do this, give our sister to a man who is uncircumcised. That would be a disgrace to us. Only on this condition will we agree to you: that you become like us, that every male among you is circumcised. Then we will give you our daughters and take your daughters for ourselves, and we will live among you and become one people. But if you will not listen to us and be circumcised, we will take our daughter and go.” And their words were good in the eyes of Hamor and of Shechem son of Hamor. And the young man did not put off doing it, because he wanted Jacob's daughter. And he was the most honored of his father's whole household.

And Hamor and Shechem his son came to the gate of their city and spoke to the men of their city: “These men are at peace with us. Let them settle in the land and trade in it — look, the land is wide enough on both sides for them. Let us take their daughters as wives for ourselves, and give them our daughters. Only on this condition will the men agree to live with us and become one people: that every male among us is circumcised, as they are circumcised. Their livestock and their property and all their animals — won't they be ours? Only let us agree to them, and they will live with us.” And everyone who went out of the gate of his city listened to Hamor and Shechem his son, and every male was circumcised, everyone who went out of the gate of his city.

And on the third day, while they were in pain, two of Jacob's sons, Simeon and Levi, Dinah's brothers, each took his sword and came into the city unopposed and killed every male. And they killed Hamor and Shechem his son with the edge of the sword, and took Dinah out of Shechem's house and left. Jacob's sons came upon the bodies and plundered the city, because they had defiled their sister. They took their flocks and their herds and their donkeys, whatever was in the city and whatever was in the field, and all their wealth. And all their little ones and their wives they took captive, and they plundered everything in the houses.

And Jacob said to Simeon and Levi, “You have brought disaster on me, made me a stench to the people of this land, to the Canaanites and the Perizzites. My men are few. They will band together against me and strike me, and I will be wiped out, I and my household.” And they said, “Should he treat our sister like a whore?”

chapters.label: Chapter 35
chapters.title: Bethel Again, and Rachel's Grave
paragraphs: And God said to Jacob, “Get up, go up to Bethel and stay there, and make an altar there to the God who appeared to you when you were running from Esau your brother.” And Jacob said to his household and to everyone who was with him, “Put away the foreign gods that are among you, and make yourselves clean, and change your clothes. And let us get up and go up to Bethel, and I will make an altar there to the God who answered me on the day of my distress, and who has been with me on the road I have traveled.” And they gave Jacob all the foreign gods that were in their hands, and the rings that were in their ears, and Jacob buried them under the oak that is near Shechem. And they set out. And a terror of God was on the cities around them, and they did not chase after Jacob's sons. And Jacob came to Luz, which is in the land of Canaan — that is, Bethel — he and all the people who were with him. And he built an altar there and called the place El-bethel, because there God had shown himself to him when he was running from his brother. And Deborah, Rebekah's nurse, died, and she was buried below Bethel, under the oak. And it was named Allon-bacuth.

And God appeared to Jacob again, when he came from Paddan-aram, and blessed him. And God said to him, “Your name is Jacob. You will no longer be called Jacob; Israel will be your name.” And he named him Israel. And God said to him, “I am El Shaddai. Be fruitful and multiply. A nation and a company of nations will come from you, and kings will come out of your loins. And the land that I gave to Abraham and to Isaac, I will give to you; and to your offspring after you I will give the land.” And God went up from him, at the place where he had spoken with him. And Jacob set up a standing stone at the place where he had spoken with him, a standing stone of rock, and he poured a drink offering on it, and poured oil on it. And Jacob named the place where God had spoken with him Bethel.

And they set out from Bethel. And when there was still some distance to go to Ephrath, Rachel went into labor, and her labor was hard. And when her labor was at its hardest, the midwife said to her, “Don't be afraid, for this one too is a son for you.” And as her life went out of her — for she was dying — she named him Ben-oni. But his father called him Benjamin. And Rachel died, and she was buried on the road to Ephrath — that is, Bethlehem. And Jacob set up a standing stone over her grave. It is the standing stone of Rachel's grave to this day.

And Israel set out and pitched his tent beyond Migdal-eder. And while Israel was living in that land, Reuben went and lay with Bilhah, his father's concubine. And Israel heard. Now the sons of Jacob were twelve. The sons of Leah: Reuben, Jacob's firstborn, and Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, and Zebulun. The sons of Rachel: Joseph and Benjamin. The sons of Bilhah, Rachel's slave: Dan and Naphtali. The sons of Zilpah, Leah's slave: Gad and Asher. These are the sons of Jacob who were born to him in Paddan-aram.

And Jacob came to Isaac his father at Mamre, at Kiriath-arba — that is, Hebron — where Abraham and Isaac had lived as strangers. And the days of Isaac were a hundred and eighty years. And Isaac breathed his last and died, and was gathered to his people, old and full of days. And Esau and Jacob his sons buried him.

chapters.label: Chapter 36
chapters.title: The Line of Esau
paragraphs: And these are the generations of Esau — that is, Edom. Esau took his wives from the women of Canaan: Adah daughter of Elon the Hittite, and Oholibamah daughter of Anah, daughter of Zibeon the Hivite, and Basemath, Ishmael's daughter, the sister of Nebaioth. And Adah bore Eliphaz to Esau, and Basemath bore Reuel, and Oholibamah bore Jeush, Jalam, and Korah. These are the sons of Esau who were born to him in the land of Canaan. And Esau took his wives and his sons and his daughters and all the people of his household, and his livestock and all his animals and all the property he had gathered in the land of Canaan, and he went to another land, away from Jacob his brother. Because what they owned was too much for them to live together, and the land where they were living as strangers could not support them, because of their livestock. So Esau settled in the hill country of Seir. Esau — that is, Edom.

And these are the generations of Esau, the father of Edom, in the hill country of Seir. These are the names of Esau's sons: Eliphaz, the son of Adah, Esau's wife; Reuel, the son of Basemath, Esau's wife. And the sons of Eliphaz were Teman, Omar, Zepho, Gatam, and Kenaz. And Timna was a concubine of Eliphaz, Esau's son, and she bore Amalek to Eliphaz. These are the sons of Adah, Esau's wife. And these are the sons of Reuel: Nahath and Zerah, Shammah and Mizzah. These were the sons of Basemath, Esau's wife. And these were the sons of Oholibamah daughter of Anah, daughter of Zibeon, Esau's wife: she bore to Esau Jeush, Jalam, and Korah.

These are the chiefs of the sons of Esau. The sons of Eliphaz, Esau's firstborn: chief Teman, chief Omar, chief Zepho, chief Kenaz, chief Korah, chief Gatam, chief Amalek. These are the chiefs of Eliphaz in the land of Edom; these are the sons of Adah. And these are the sons of Reuel, Esau's son: chief Nahath, chief Zerah, chief Shammah, chief Mizzah. These are the chiefs of Reuel in the land of Edom; these are the sons of Basemath, Esau's wife. And these are the sons of Oholibamah, Esau's wife: chief Jeush, chief Jalam, chief Korah. These are the chiefs of Oholibamah daughter of Anah, Esau's wife. These are the sons of Esau, and these are their chiefs — that is, Edom.

These are the sons of Seir the Horite, who were living in the land: Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah, Dishon, Ezer, and Dishan. These are the chiefs of the Horites, the sons of Seir, in the land of Edom. And the sons of Lotan were Hori and Hemam, and Lotan's sister was Timna. And these are the sons of Shobal: Alvan, Manahath, Ebal, Shepho, and Onam. And these are the sons of Zibeon: Aiah and Anah. He is the Anah who found the yemim in the wilderness, while he was pasturing the donkeys of Zibeon his father. And these are the children of Anah: Dishon, and Oholibamah daughter of Anah. And these are the sons of Dishan: Hemdan, Eshban, Ithran, and Cheran. These are the sons of Ezer: Bilhan, Zaavan, and Akan. These are the sons of Dishan: Uz and Aran. These are the chiefs of the Horites: chief Lotan, chief Shobal, chief Zibeon, chief Anah, chief Dishon, chief Ezer, chief Dishan. These are the chiefs of the Horites, chief by chief, in the land of Seir.

And these are the kings who reigned in the land of Edom before any king reigned over the Israelites. Bela son of Beor reigned in Edom, and the name of his city was Dinhabah. And Bela died, and Jobab son of Zerah, from Bozrah, reigned in his place. And Jobab died, and Husham, from the land of the Temanites, reigned in his place. And Husham died, and Hadad son of Bedad, who struck down Midian in the country of Moab, reigned in his place; and the name of his city was Avith. And Hadad died, and Samlah, from Masrekah, reigned in his place. And Samlah died, and Shaul, from Rehoboth-on-the-River, reigned in his place. And Shaul died, and Baal-hanan son of Achbor reigned in his place. And Baal-hanan son of Achbor died, and Hadar reigned in his place; and the name of his city was Pau, and his wife's name was Mehetabel daughter of Matred, daughter of Me-zahab.

And these are the names of the chiefs of Esau, by their clans and their places, by their names: chief Timna, chief Alvah, chief Jetheth, chief Oholibamah, chief Elah, chief Pinon, chief Kenaz, chief Teman, chief Mibzar, chief Magdiel, chief Iram. These are the chiefs of Edom, by their settlements in the land they held. This is Esau, the father of Edom.

chapters.label: Chapter 37
chapters.title: The Dreamer and the Coat
paragraphs: And Jacob settled in the land where his father had lived as a stranger, in the land of Canaan. These are the generations of Jacob. Joseph, seventeen years old, was pasturing the flock with his brothers — he was a boy among the sons of Bilhah and the sons of Zilpah, his father's wives — and Joseph brought a bad report of them to their father. Now Israel loved Joseph more than all his sons, because he was the son of his old age, and he made him an ornamented coat. And his brothers saw that their father loved him more than all his brothers, and they hated him, and could not speak a peaceful word to him.

And Joseph dreamed a dream and told it to his brothers, and they hated him even more. And he said to them, “Listen to this dream I dreamed. There we were, binding sheaves in the middle of the field, and my sheaf rose and stood up straight, and your sheaves gathered around and bowed down to my sheaf.” And his brothers said to him, “Are you really going to be king over us? Are you really going to rule us?” And they hated him even more, for his dreams and for his words. And he dreamed another dream and told it to his brothers. He said, “Look, I dreamed another dream — and there were the sun and the moon and eleven stars, bowing down to me.” And he told it to his father and to his brothers, and his father rebuked him and said to him, “What is this dream you dreamed? Are we really going to come, I and your mother and your brothers, and bow to the ground before you?” And his brothers were jealous of him, but his father kept the thing in mind.

And his brothers went to pasture their father's flock at Shechem. And Israel said to Joseph, “Aren't your brothers pasturing at Shechem? Come, I will send you to them.” And he said to him, “Here I am.” And he said to him, “Go and see whether all is well with your brothers and well with the flock, and bring me back word.” So he sent him from the valley of Hebron, and he came to Shechem. And a man found him — there he was, wandering in the field — and the man asked him, “What are you looking for?” And he said, “I am looking for my brothers. Tell me, please, where they are pasturing.” And the man said, “They have moved on from here. I heard them say, ‘Let's go to Dothan.’” So Joseph went after his brothers and found them at Dothan.

And they saw him from a distance, and before he came near them they plotted against him, to put him to death. And they said to one another, “Here comes that master of dreams. Come on, let's kill him and throw him into one of the pits, and we will say a vicious animal ate him. Then we will see what becomes of his dreams.” And Reuben heard, and he saved him from their hands. He said, “Let's not take his life.” And Reuben said to them, “Shed no blood. Throw him into this pit here in the wilderness, but do not lay a hand on him” — so that he could save him from their hands and bring him back to his father. And when Joseph came to his brothers, they stripped Joseph of his coat, the ornamented coat he had on. And they took him and threw him into the pit. And the pit was empty; there was no water in it.

And they sat down to eat bread. And they looked up and saw — there was a caravan of Ishmaelites coming from Gilead, their camels carrying gum and balm and resin, on their way to take it down to Egypt. And Judah said to his brothers, “What do we gain if we kill our brother and cover up his blood? Come, let's sell him to the Ishmaelites, and let our hand not be on him, because he is our brother, our own flesh.” And his brothers listened. And Midianite men, traders, passed by, and they pulled Joseph up and lifted him out of the pit, and they sold Joseph to the Ishmaelites for twenty pieces of silver. And they brought Joseph to Egypt. And Reuben came back to the pit — and Joseph was not in the pit. And he tore his clothes. And he went back to his brothers and said, “The boy is gone! And I — where am I to go?”

And they took Joseph's coat, and slaughtered a goat, and dipped the coat in the blood. And they sent the ornamented coat and had it brought to their father, and they said, “We found this. Recognize it, please: is it your son's coat or not?” And he recognized it and said, “My son's coat! A vicious animal has eaten him. Joseph is torn, torn to pieces.” And Jacob tore his clothes and put sackcloth on his waist, and he mourned for his son many days. And all his sons and all his daughters rose to comfort him, but he refused to be comforted, and said, “No — I will go down to my son in Sheol, mourning.” And his father wept for him. And the Medanites sold him into Egypt, to Potiphar, a court official of Pharaoh, the captain of the guard.

chapters.label: Chapter 38
chapters.title: Judah and Tamar
paragraphs: And at that time Judah went down from his brothers and turned aside to an Adullamite man whose name was Hirah. And there Judah saw the daughter of a Canaanite man whose name was Shua, and he took her and went in to her. And she conceived and bore a son, and he named him Er. And she conceived again and bore a son, and she named him Onan. And once more she bore a son, and she named him Shelah. He was at Chezib when she bore him. And Judah took a wife for Er his firstborn, and her name was Tamar. But Er, Judah's firstborn, was evil in the eyes of the LORD, and the LORD put him to death. And Judah said to Onan, “Go in to your brother's wife and do a brother-in-law's duty by her, and raise up offspring for your brother.” But Onan knew the offspring would not be his. So whenever he went in to his brother's wife he wasted it on the ground, so as not to give offspring to his brother. And what he did was evil in the eyes of the LORD, and he put him to death too. And Judah said to Tamar his daughter-in-law, “Stay a widow in your father's house until Shelah my son grows up” — because he thought, “He might die too, like his brothers.” So Tamar went and stayed in her father's house.

And many days passed, and Shua's daughter, Judah's wife, died. And when Judah was comforted, he went up to his sheepshearers at Timnah, he and his friend Hirah the Adullamite. And Tamar was told, “Look, your father-in-law is going up to Timnah to shear his sheep.” And she took off her widow's clothes and covered herself with a veil and wrapped herself up, and she sat at the entrance to Enaim, which is on the road to Timnah — because she saw that Shelah had grown up, and she had not been given to him as a wife. And Judah saw her and took her for a whore, because she had covered her face. And he turned aside to her by the road and said, “Come, please, let me come in to you” — because he did not know she was his daughter-in-law. And she said, “What will you give me to come in to me?” And he said, “I will send a kid from the flock.” And she said, “Only if you give a pledge until you send it.” And he said, “What pledge should I give you?” And she said, “Your seal and your cord, and the staff in your hand.” And he gave them to her and went in to her, and she conceived by him. And she got up and went, and she took off her veil and put on her widow's clothes.

And Judah sent the kid by the hand of his friend the Adullamite, to get the pledge back from the woman's hand, and he did not find her. And he asked the men of her place, “Where is the consecrated woman, the one at Enaim by the road?” And they said, “There has been no consecrated woman here.” And he went back to Judah and said, “I did not find her. And the men of the place also said, ‘There has been no consecrated woman here.’” And Judah said, “Let her keep them, or we will be a laughingstock. Look, I sent this kid, and you did not find her.”

And about three months later Judah was told, “Tamar your daughter-in-law has played the whore, and look — she is pregnant by her whoring.” And Judah said, “Bring her out and let her be burned.” As she was being brought out, she sent word to her father-in-law: “By the man these belong to, I am pregnant.” And she said, “Recognize, please, whose these are — the seal and the cords and the staff.” And Judah recognized them and said, “She is more in the right than I am, because I did not give her to Shelah my son.” And he did not know her again.

And when the time came for her to give birth — there were twins in her womb. And as she was giving birth, one put out a hand, and the midwife took a crimson thread and tied it on his hand, saying, “This one came out first.” But as he drew back his hand — out came his brother. And she said, “What a breach you have made for yourself!” And he was named Perez. And afterward his brother came out, the one with the crimson on his hand, and he was named Zerah.

chapters.label: Chapter 39
chapters.title: In the Egyptian's House
paragraphs: And Joseph was taken down to Egypt. And Potiphar, a court official of Pharaoh, the captain of the guard, an Egyptian man, bought him from the hand of the Ishmaelites who had brought him down there. And the LORD was with Joseph, and he was a man who succeeded, and he was in the house of his Egyptian master. And his master saw that the LORD was with him, and that everything he did the LORD made succeed in his hand. And Joseph found favor in his eyes and attended him. And he put him in charge of his house, and everything he had he put in his hand. And from the time he put him in charge of his house and of everything he had, the LORD blessed the Egyptian's house because of Joseph, and the blessing of the LORD was on everything he had, in the house and in the field. And he left everything he had in Joseph's hand, and with him there he gave no thought to anything except the bread he ate. Now Joseph was well built and beautiful.

And after these things his master's wife raised her eyes to Joseph and said, “Lie with me.” And he refused. He said to his master's wife, “Look, with me here my master gives no thought to anything in the house, and everything he has he has put in my hand. No one is greater in this house than I am, and he has held back nothing from me except you, because you are his wife. How could I do this great evil, and sin against God?” And though she spoke to Joseph day after day, he would not listen to her, to lie beside her, to be with her. And on one such day he came into the house to do his work, and none of the men of the household was there in the house. And she caught hold of him by his garment and said, “Lie with me.” And he left his garment in her hand and fled, and went outside.

And when she saw that he had left his garment in her hand and fled outside, she called to the men of her household and said to them, “See — he brought us a Hebrew man to play with us. He came in to me to lie with me, and I screamed. And when he heard me raise my voice and scream, he left his garment beside me and fled, and went outside.” And she kept his garment beside her until his master came home. And she told him the same story: “The Hebrew slave you brought us came in to me to play with me. And when I raised my voice and screamed, he left his garment beside me and fled outside.”

And when his master heard the words his wife spoke to him — “This is what your slave did to me” — his anger flared. And Joseph's master took him and put him in the prison, the place where the king's prisoners were confined. And he was there in the prison. And the LORD was with Joseph and showed him kindness, and gave him favor in the eyes of the warden of the prison. And the warden put all the prisoners in the prison in Joseph's hand, and whatever was done there, he was the one who did it. The warden did not look into anything at all that was in his hand, because the LORD was with him; and whatever he did, the LORD made succeed.

chapters.label: Chapter 40
chapters.title: The Cupbearer and the Baker
paragraphs: And after these things the cupbearer of the king of Egypt and the baker offended their lord, the king of Egypt. And Pharaoh was furious with his two officials, the chief cupbearer and the chief baker, and he put them under guard in the house of the captain of the guard, in the prison, the place where Joseph was confined. And the captain of the guard assigned Joseph to them, and he attended them. And they were under guard for some time.

And the two of them dreamed a dream, each his own dream, in a single night, each dream with its own meaning — the cupbearer and the baker of the king of Egypt, who were confined in the prison. And Joseph came to them in the morning and saw them — and they were troubled. And he asked Pharaoh's officials who were with him under guard in his master's house, “Why are your faces so dark today?” And they said to him, “We dreamed a dream, and there is no one to interpret it.” And Joseph said to them, “Don't interpretations belong to God? Tell me, please.”

And the chief cupbearer told his dream to Joseph. He said to him, “In my dream — there was a vine in front of me, and on the vine three branches. And as it budded, its blossoms came out, and its clusters ripened into grapes. And Pharaoh's cup was in my hand, and I took the grapes and squeezed them into Pharaoh's cup, and I put the cup in Pharaoh's palm.” And Joseph said to him, “This is its meaning. The three branches are three days. In three days Pharaoh will lift up your head and put you back in your post, and you will put Pharaoh's cup in his hand, as you used to do when you were his cupbearer. But remember me when it goes well with you, and please show me kindness: mention me to Pharaoh, and get me out of this house. For I was stolen, stolen from the land of the Hebrews, and here too I have done nothing that they should have put me in the pit.”

And the chief baker saw that he had interpreted well, and he said to Joseph, “I too, in my dream — there were three baskets of white bread on my head. And in the top basket there was every kind of food for Pharaoh, baker's work, and the birds were eating it out of the basket on my head.” And Joseph answered, “This is its meaning. The three baskets are three days. In three days Pharaoh will lift up your head — off you — and hang you on a tree, and the birds will eat your flesh off you.”

And on the third day, Pharaoh's birthday, he made a feast for all his servants, and he lifted up the head of the chief cupbearer and the head of the chief baker among his servants. And he put the chief cupbearer back in his cupbearing, and he put the cup in Pharaoh's palm. But the chief baker he hanged, as Joseph had interpreted for them. And the chief cupbearer did not remember Joseph. He forgot him.

chapters.label: Chapter 41
chapters.title: Pharaoh's Dreams
paragraphs: And at the end of two full years Pharaoh dreamed — and there he was, standing by the Nile. And out of the Nile came up seven cows, fine-looking and fat, and they grazed among the reeds. And seven other cows came up after them out of the Nile, ugly and gaunt, and they stood beside the cows on the bank of the Nile. And the ugly, gaunt cows ate the seven fine-looking, fat cows. And Pharaoh woke up. And he slept and dreamed a second time — and there were seven ears of grain coming up on a single stalk, fat and good. And seven ears, thin and scorched by the east wind, sprouted after them. And the thin ears swallowed the seven fat, full ears. And Pharaoh woke up — and it was a dream. And in the morning his spirit was troubled, and he sent and called all the magicians of Egypt and all its wise men. And Pharaoh told them his dream, and there was no one who could interpret them for Pharaoh.

And the chief cupbearer spoke to Pharaoh: “Today I bring up my offenses. Pharaoh was furious with his servants, and he put me under guard in the house of the captain of the guard, me and the chief baker.
