And we dreamed a dream in a single night, he and I, each of us a dream with its own meaning. And there with us was a Hebrew boy, a slave of the captain of the guard. We told him, and he interpreted our dreams for us; he interpreted for each of us according to his dream. And just as he interpreted for us, so it was: me he put back in my post, and him he hanged.”

And Pharaoh sent and called Joseph, and they rushed him out of the pit. And he shaved and changed his clothes and came to Pharaoh. And Pharaoh said to Joseph, “I dreamed a dream, and there is no one to interpret it. And I have heard it said of you that you hear a dream and can interpret it.” And Joseph answered Pharaoh, “Not I. God will give an answer for Pharaoh's well-being.” And Pharaoh said to Joseph, “In my dream — there I was, standing on the bank of the Nile. And out of the Nile came up seven cows, fat and fine-looking, and they grazed among the reeds. And seven other cows came up after them, scrawny and very ugly and lean — I have never seen any as ugly in all the land of Egypt. And the lean, ugly cows ate the first seven cows, the fat ones. And they went into their bellies, and you could not tell that they had gone into their bellies: they looked as ugly as before. And I woke up. And I saw in my dream — there were seven ears of grain coming up on a single stalk, full and good. And seven ears, withered, thin, scorched by the east wind, sprouted after them. And the thin ears swallowed the seven good ears. And I told the magicians, and no one could explain it to me.”

And Joseph said to Pharaoh, “Pharaoh's dream is one. What God is about to do, he has told Pharaoh. The seven good cows are seven years, and the seven good ears are seven years. It is one dream. And the seven lean, ugly cows that came up after them are seven years, and so are the seven empty ears scorched by the east wind: they will be seven years of famine. It is as I said to Pharaoh: what God is about to do, he has shown Pharaoh. Look — seven years are coming of great plenty in all the land of Egypt. And after them seven years of famine will arise, and all the plenty in the land of Egypt will be forgotten, and the famine will consume the land. And the plenty will not be known in the land because of the famine that follows, for it will be very heavy. And as for the dream coming to Pharaoh twice — the thing is fixed by God, and God is hurrying to do it. So now let Pharaoh look for a man who is discerning and wise, and set him over the land of Egypt. Let Pharaoh act and appoint overseers over the land, and take a fifth from the land of Egypt in the seven years of plenty. Let them gather all the food of these good years that are coming, and pile up grain under Pharaoh's hand as food in the cities, and guard it. And the food will be a reserve for the land against the seven years of famine that will come on the land of Egypt, so the land is not cut off by the famine.”

And the thing was good in the eyes of Pharaoh and in the eyes of all his servants. And Pharaoh said to his servants, “Can we find a man like this, one in whom is the spirit of God?” And Pharaoh said to Joseph, “Since God has made all this known to you, there is no one as discerning and wise as you. You will be over my house, and by your word all my people will be led. Only by the throne will I be greater than you.” And Pharaoh said to Joseph, “See, I have set you over all the land of Egypt.” And Pharaoh took his signet ring off his hand and put it on Joseph's hand, and he dressed him in garments of fine linen and put the gold chain on his neck. And he had him ride in the chariot of his second-in-command, and they called out before him, “Abrek!” So he set him over all the land of Egypt. And Pharaoh said to Joseph, “I am Pharaoh; and without you no man will lift his hand or his foot in all the land of Egypt.” And Pharaoh named Joseph Zaphenath-paneah, and he gave him Asenath, daughter of Potiphera, priest of On, as a wife. And Joseph went out over the land of Egypt.

Joseph was thirty years old when he stood before Pharaoh king of Egypt. And Joseph went out from Pharaoh's presence and passed through all the land of Egypt. And in the seven years of plenty the land produced by handfuls. And he gathered all the food of the seven years that were in the land of Egypt, and he put food in the cities: the food of the fields around each city he put inside it. And Joseph piled up grain like the sand of the sea, a great deal of it, until he stopped counting, because it could not be counted. And before the year of famine came, two sons were born to Joseph, whom Asenath, daughter of Potiphera, priest of On, bore to him. And Joseph named the firstborn Manasseh — “because God has made me forget all my hardship, and all my father's house.” And the second he named Ephraim — “because God has made me fruitful in the land of my misery.”

And the seven years of plenty that were in the land of Egypt came to an end, and the seven years of famine began to come, as Joseph had said. And there was famine in all the lands, but in all the land of Egypt there was bread. And all the land of Egypt went hungry, and the people cried out to Pharaoh for bread. And Pharaoh said to all Egypt, “Go to Joseph. Whatever he tells you, do.” And the famine was over the whole face of the earth. And Joseph opened all that was in them and sold grain to Egypt, and the famine grew severe in the land of Egypt. And all the earth came to Egypt to buy grain, to Joseph, because the famine was severe over all the earth.

chapters.label: Chapter 42
chapters.title: The Brothers Come Down
paragraphs: And Jacob saw that there was grain in Egypt, and Jacob said to his sons, “Why do you keep looking at one another?” And he said, “Look, I have heard there is grain in Egypt. Go down there and buy for us from there, so that we live and do not die.” And ten of Joseph's brothers went down to buy grain from Egypt. But Benjamin, Joseph's brother, Jacob did not send with his brothers, because he said, “Harm might come to him.” So the sons of Israel came to buy among the others who came, because the famine was in the land of Canaan.

Now Joseph was the governor over the land; he was the one who sold grain to all the people of the land. And Joseph's brothers came and bowed to him with their faces to the ground. And Joseph saw his brothers and recognized them, but he made himself a stranger to them and spoke harshly to them. He said to them, “Where have you come from?” And they said, “From the land of Canaan, to buy food.” And Joseph recognized his brothers, but they did not recognize him. And Joseph remembered the dreams he had dreamed about them, and he said to them, “You are spies. You have come to see the nakedness of the land.” And they said to him, “No, my lord. Your servants have come to buy food. We are all sons of one man. We are honest men. Your servants have never been spies.” And he said to them, “No — you have come to see the nakedness of the land.” And they said, “Your servants are twelve brothers, sons of one man in the land of Canaan. The youngest is with our father today, and one is no more.” And Joseph said to them, “It is just as I told you: you are spies. By this you will be tested: as Pharaoh lives, you will not leave here unless your youngest brother comes here. Send one of you to get your brother, while the rest of you stay confined, and your words will be tested, whether the truth is with you. And if not — as Pharaoh lives, you are spies.” And he put them all under guard for three days.

And on the third day Joseph said to them, “Do this and live, for I fear God. If you are honest men, let one of your brothers stay confined in the house where you are under guard, and the rest of you go, and carry grain for the hunger of your households. And bring your youngest brother to me, so your words will be proved true and you will not die.” And they did so. And they said to one another, “Truly we are guilty over our brother. We saw his distress when he pleaded with us, and we did not listen. That is why this distress has come on us.” And Reuben answered them, “Didn't I tell you, ‘Do not sin against the boy’? And you would not listen. And now his blood is being called to account.” And they did not know that Joseph understood, because the interpreter was between them. And he turned away from them and wept. Then he came back to them and spoke to them, and he took Simeon from them and bound him before their eyes.

And Joseph gave orders to fill their bags with grain, and to put each man's silver back in his sack, and to give them provisions for the road. And so it was done for them. And they loaded their grain on their donkeys and went from there. And at the lodging place one of them opened his sack to give his donkey fodder, and he saw his silver — there it was, in the mouth of his pack. And he said to his brothers, “My silver has been put back. Look, it's here in my pack!” And their hearts gave out, and they turned trembling to one another and said, “What is this that God has done to us?”

And they came to Jacob their father in the land of Canaan and told him everything that had happened to them: “The man, the lord of the land, spoke harshly to us and took us for men spying on the land. And we said to him, ‘We are honest men. We have never been spies. We are twelve brothers, sons of our father. One is no more, and the youngest is with our father today in the land of Canaan.’ And the man, the lord of the land, said to us, ‘By this I will know that you are honest men: leave one of your brothers with me, and take grain for the hunger of your households, and go. And bring your youngest brother to me, and I will know that you are not spies, that you are honest men. I will give your brother back to you, and you may trade in the land.’”

And as they were emptying their sacks — there was each man's pouch of silver in his sack. And they saw their pouches of silver, they and their father, and they were afraid. And Jacob their father said to them, “You have left me childless. Joseph is no more, and Simeon is no more, and now you would take Benjamin. It all falls on me.” And Reuben said to his father, “You may put my two sons to death if I do not bring him back to you. Put him in my hand, and I will return him to you.” And he said, “My son will not go down with you. His brother is dead, and he alone is left. If harm comes to him on the road you travel, you will bring my gray head down to Sheol in grief.”

chapters.label: Chapter 43
chapters.title: Benjamin
paragraphs: And the famine was heavy in the land. And when they had finished eating the grain they had brought from Egypt, their father said to them, “Go back, buy us a little food.” And Judah said to him, “The man warned us solemnly: ‘You will not see my face unless your brother is with you.’ If you will send our brother with us, we will go down and buy food for you. But if you will not send him, we will not go down, because the man said to us, ‘You will not see my face unless your brother is with you.’” And Israel said, “Why did you do me this harm, telling the man you had another brother?” And they said, “The man kept asking about us and about our family: ‘Is your father still alive? Do you have a brother?’ And we told him what he asked. How could we know he would say, ‘Bring your brother down’?” And Judah said to Israel his father, “Send the boy with me, and let us get up and go, so that we live and do not die — we, and you, and our little ones. I myself will be his pledge. From my hand you may demand him. If I do not bring him back to you and set him in front of you, I will bear the blame before you all my days. If we had not lingered, we could have been there and back twice by now.”

And Israel their father said to them, “If it must be so, then do this: take some of the best the land yields in your bags, and carry a gift down to the man — a little balm and a little honey, gum and resin, pistachios and almonds. And take double the silver in your hand, and the silver that was put back in the mouths of your packs, take back in your hand. Maybe it was a mistake. And take your brother. Get up, go back to the man. And may El Shaddai give you compassion before the man, so that he sends back your other brother, and Benjamin. As for me — if I am bereaved, I am bereaved.”

And the men took this gift, and they took double the silver in their hand, and Benjamin, and they got up and went down to Egypt and stood before Joseph. And Joseph saw Benjamin with them, and he said to the one in charge of his house, “Bring the men into the house, and slaughter an animal and prepare it, because the men will eat with me at noon.” And the man did as Joseph said, and the man brought the men into Joseph's house. And the men were afraid at being brought into Joseph's house, and they said, “It is because of the silver that came back in our packs the first time that we are being brought in — to fall on us and overpower us and take us as slaves, with our donkeys.” And they came up to the man in charge of Joseph's house and spoke to him at the entrance of the house. They said, “Please, my lord — we came down the first time to buy food. And when we came to the lodging place and opened our packs, there was each man's silver in the mouth of his pack, our silver in full weight. We have brought it back in our hand. And we have brought down other silver in our hand to buy food. We do not know who put our silver in our packs.” And he said, “Peace to you. Do not be afraid. Your God, the God of your father, gave you treasure in your packs. Your silver came to me.” And he brought Simeon out to them.

And the man brought the men into Joseph's house and gave them water, and they washed their feet, and he gave fodder to their donkeys. And they laid out the gift for Joseph's coming at noon, because they had heard they were to eat bread there. And Joseph came home, and they brought him the gift that was in their hand, into the house, and they bowed to the ground before him. And he asked how they were, and said, “Is your father well, the old man you spoke of? Is he still alive?” And they said, “Your servant our father is well. He is still alive.” And they bowed their heads and bowed down. And he looked up and saw Benjamin his brother, his mother's son, and said, “Is this your youngest brother, the one you spoke of to me?” And he said, “God be gracious to you, my son.” And Joseph hurried out, because his compassion for his brother burned in him and he wanted to weep, and he went into an inner room and wept there. Then he washed his face and came out, and he held himself in and said, “Serve the bread.”

And they served him by himself, and them by themselves, and the Egyptians who ate with him by themselves — because Egyptians cannot eat bread with Hebrews; that is an abomination to Egyptians. And they were seated in front of him, the firstborn according to his birthright and the youngest according to his youth, and the men looked at one another in amazement. And portions were carried to them from in front of him, and Benjamin's portion was five times larger than any of theirs. And they drank, and drank deep with him.

chapters.label: Chapter 44
chapters.title: The Silver Cup
paragraphs: And he commanded the one in charge of his house: “Fill the men's packs with food, as much as they can carry, and put each man's silver in the mouth of his pack. And my cup, the silver cup, put in the mouth of the youngest one's pack, with the silver for his grain.” And he did as Joseph told him. At morning light the men were sent off, they and their donkeys. They had left the city and had not gone far when Joseph said to the one in charge of his house, “Get up, chase after the men, and when you catch up with them say to them, ‘Why have you repaid evil for good? Isn't this the one my lord drinks from, and uses for divination? What you have done is evil.’”

And he caught up with them and spoke these words to them. And they said to him, “Why does my lord say such things? Far be it from your servants to do a thing like this. Look, the silver we found in the mouths of our packs we brought back to you from the land of Canaan. How then would we steal silver or gold from your lord's house? Whichever of your servants it is found with, he will die, and we ourselves will be my lord's slaves.” And he said, “Very well, let it be as you say: the one it is found with will be my slave, and the rest of you will be clear.” And each of them hurried to lower his pack to the ground, and each opened his pack. And he searched, beginning with the oldest and ending with the youngest, and the cup was found in Benjamin's pack. And they tore their clothes, and each loaded his donkey, and they went back to the city.

And Judah and his brothers came into Joseph's house — he was still there — and they fell to the ground before him. And Joseph said to them, “What is this thing you have done? Didn't you know that a man like me practices divination?” And Judah said, “What can we say to my lord? What can we speak? How can we clear ourselves? God has found out your servants' guilt. Here we are, my lord's slaves, both we and the one in whose hand the cup was found.” And he said, “Far be it from me to do that. The man in whose hand the cup was found, he will be my slave. As for the rest of you, go up in peace to your father.”

And Judah came near him and said, “Please, my lord, let your servant speak a word in my lord's ears, and do not let your anger flare against your servant, for you are like Pharaoh himself. My lord asked his servants, ‘Do you have a father, or a brother?’ And we said to my lord, ‘We have an old father, and a young child of his old age. His brother is dead, and he alone is left of his mother, and his father loves him.’ And you said to your servants, ‘Bring him down to me, so I may set my eyes on him.’ And we said to my lord, ‘The boy cannot leave his father. If he left his father, his father would die.’ And you said to your servants, ‘Unless your youngest brother comes down with you, you will not see my face again.’ And when we went up to your servant my father, we told him my lord's words. And our father said, ‘Go back, buy us a little food.’ And we said, ‘We cannot go down. If our youngest brother is with us, we will go down; for we cannot see the man's face unless our youngest brother is with us.’ And your servant my father said to us, ‘You know that my wife bore me two sons. One went out from me, and I said: Surely he is torn, torn to pieces. And I have not seen him since. If you take this one from me too, and harm comes to him, you will bring my gray head down to Sheol in misery.’

“And now, if I come to your servant my father and the boy is not with us — and his life is bound up with the boy's life — then when he sees that the boy is not there, he will die, and your servants will bring the gray head of your servant our father down to Sheol in grief. For your servant became a pledge for the boy to my father, saying, ‘If I do not bring him back to you, I will bear the blame before my father all my days.’ So now, please, let your servant stay instead of the boy as my lord's slave, and let the boy go up with his brothers. For how can I go up to my father if the boy is not with me? Let me not see the evil that would find my father.”

chapters.label: Chapter 45
chapters.title: I Am Joseph
paragraphs: And Joseph could no longer hold himself in before all who stood around him, and he called out, “Send everyone out from me!” So no one stood with him when Joseph made himself known to his brothers. And he gave his voice to weeping, and the Egyptians heard, and Pharaoh's house heard. And Joseph said to his brothers, “I am Joseph. Is my father still alive?” And his brothers could not answer him, because they were terrified before him. And Joseph said to his brothers, “Come near me, please.” And they came near. And he said, “I am Joseph your brother, whom you sold into Egypt. And now, do not be grieved, and do not be angry with yourselves that you sold me here, because it was to save life that God sent me ahead of you. For two years now the famine has been in the land, and there are five more years with no plowing and no harvest. And God sent me ahead of you to make you a remnant on the earth, and to keep you alive as a great band of survivors. So now, it was not you who sent me here, but God. And he has made me a father to Pharaoh, and lord of all his house, and ruler over all the land of Egypt.

“Hurry and go up to my father and say to him, ‘This is what your son Joseph says: God has made me lord of all Egypt. Come down to me; do not delay. You will live in the land of Goshen, and you will be near me — you and your sons and your sons' sons, your flocks and your herds and all that you have. And I will provide for you there, for there are still five years of famine — so that you do not come to poverty, you and your household and all that you have.’ And look, your eyes see, and the eyes of my brother Benjamin see, that it is my own mouth speaking to you. And tell my father of all my honor in Egypt, and all that you have seen, and hurry and bring my father down here.” And he fell on the neck of Benjamin his brother and wept, and Benjamin wept on his neck. And he kissed all his brothers and wept over them. And after that his brothers spoke with him.

And the news was heard in Pharaoh's house: “Joseph's brothers have come.” And it was good in the eyes of Pharaoh and in the eyes of his servants. And Pharaoh said to Joseph, “Say to your brothers, ‘Do this: load your animals and go, get to the land of Canaan, and take your father and your households and come to me. I will give you the best of the land of Egypt, and you will eat the fat of the land.’ And you are commanded: ‘Do this: take wagons from the land of Egypt for your little ones and your wives, and carry your father, and come. And do not let your eye regret your belongings, for the best of all the land of Egypt is yours.’”

And the sons of Israel did so. And Joseph gave them wagons at Pharaoh's order, and gave them provisions for the road. To each of them he gave a change of clothes, but to Benjamin he gave three hundred pieces of silver and five changes of clothes. And to his father he sent this: ten donkeys carrying the best of Egypt, and ten female donkeys carrying grain and bread and food for his father for the road. And he sent his brothers off, and they went, and he said to them, “Do not be stirred up on the road.”

And they went up from Egypt and came to the land of Canaan, to Jacob their father. And they told him, “Joseph is still alive, and he is ruler over all the land of Egypt!” And his heart went numb, because he did not believe them. And they told him all the words Joseph had spoken to them, and he saw the wagons Joseph had sent to carry him, and the spirit of Jacob their father came back to life. And Israel said, “Enough. Joseph my son is still alive. I will go and see him before I die.”

chapters.label: Chapter 46
chapters.title: Down to Egypt
paragraphs: And Israel set out with everything he had and came to Beersheba, and he offered sacrifices to the God of his father Isaac. And God spoke to Israel in visions of the night and said, “Jacob! Jacob!” And he said, “Here I am.” And he said, “I am God, the God of your father. Do not be afraid to go down to Egypt, for I will make you a great nation there. I myself will go down with you to Egypt, and I myself will surely bring you up again; and Joseph will lay his hand on your eyes.” And Jacob set out from Beersheba, and the sons of Israel carried Jacob their father and their little ones and their wives in the wagons Pharaoh had sent to carry him. And they took their livestock and the property they had gathered in the land of Canaan, and they came to Egypt, Jacob and all his offspring with him: his sons and his sons' sons with him, his daughters and his sons' daughters — all his offspring he brought with him to Egypt.

And these are the names of the sons of Israel who came to Egypt, Jacob and his sons. Jacob's firstborn: Reuben. And the sons of Reuben: Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi. And the sons of Simeon: Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jachin, Zohar, and Shaul, the son of a Canaanite woman. And the sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari. And the sons of Judah: Er, Onan, Shelah, Perez, and Zerah; but Er and Onan died in the land of Canaan. And the sons of Perez were Hezron and Hamul. And the sons of Issachar: Tola, Puvah, Iob, and Shimron. And the sons of Zebulun: Sered, Elon, and Jahleel. These are the sons of Leah, whom she bore to Jacob in Paddan-aram, and Dinah his daughter as well. All his sons and his daughters: thirty-three persons.

And the sons of Gad: Ziphion, Haggi, Shuni, Ezbon, Eri, Arodi, and Areli. And the sons of Asher: Imnah, Ishvah, Ishvi, and Beriah, and Serah their sister. And the sons of Beriah: Heber and Malchiel. These are the sons of Zilpah, whom Laban gave to Leah his daughter; she bore these to Jacob — sixteen persons.

The sons of Rachel, Jacob's wife: Joseph and Benjamin. And to Joseph in the land of Egypt were born Manasseh and Ephraim, whom Asenath, daughter of Potiphera, priest of On, bore to him. And the sons of Benjamin: Bela, Becher, Ashbel, Gera, Naaman, Ehi, Rosh, Muppim, Huppim, and Ard. These are the sons of Rachel who were born to Jacob — fourteen persons in all.

And the sons of Dan: Hushim. And the sons of Naphtali: Jahzeel, Guni, Jezer, and Shillem. These are the sons of Bilhah, whom Laban gave to Rachel his daughter; she bore these to Jacob — seven persons in all. All the persons belonging to Jacob who came to Egypt, who came out of his loins, not counting the wives of Jacob's sons — sixty-six persons in all. And the sons of Joseph who were born to him in Egypt: two persons. All the persons of the house of Jacob who came to Egypt: seventy.

And he sent Judah ahead of him to Joseph, to show the way before him to Goshen, and they came to the land of Goshen. And Joseph harnessed his chariot and went up to meet Israel his father in Goshen. And he appeared before him and fell on his neck, and wept on his neck a long time. And Israel said to Joseph, “Now I can die, after seeing your face, since you are still alive.” And Joseph said to his brothers and to his father's household, “I will go up and tell Pharaoh, and say to him, ‘My brothers and my father's household, who were in the land of Canaan, have come to me. And the men are shepherds, for they have always been keepers of livestock, and they have brought their flocks and their herds and all that they have.’ And when Pharaoh calls you and says, ‘What is your work?’ you are to say, ‘Your servants have been keepers of livestock from our youth until now, both we and our fathers’ — so that you may live in the land of Goshen. For every shepherd is an abomination to Egyptians.”

chapters.label: Chapter 47
chapters.title: Jacob Before Pharaoh, and the Famine
paragraphs: And Joseph came and told Pharaoh, “My father and my brothers, with their flocks and their herds and all that they have, have come from the land of Canaan, and here they are in the land of Goshen.” And from among his brothers he took five men and set them before Pharaoh. And Pharaoh said to his brothers, “What is your work?” And they said to Pharaoh, “Your servants are shepherds, both we and our fathers.” And they said to Pharaoh, “We have come to stay a while in the land, because there is no pasture for your servants' flocks, for the famine is heavy in the land of Canaan. So now, please let your servants live in the land of Goshen.” And Pharaoh said to Joseph, “Your father and your brothers have come to you. The land of Egypt is in front of you. Settle your father and your brothers in the best of the land. Let them live in the land of Goshen. And if you know of capable men among them, put them in charge of my own livestock.”

And Joseph brought Jacob his father and stood him before Pharaoh, and Jacob blessed Pharaoh. And Pharaoh said to Jacob, “How many are the days of the years of your life?” And Jacob said to Pharaoh, “The days of the years of my life as a stranger are a hundred and thirty years. Few and hard have been the days of the years of my life, and they have not reached the days of the years of my fathers' lives, in the days when they lived as strangers.” And Jacob blessed Pharaoh, and went out from Pharaoh's presence. And Joseph settled his father and his brothers and gave them a holding in the land of Egypt, in the best of the land, in the land of Rameses, as Pharaoh had commanded. And Joseph provided his father and his brothers and all his father's household with bread, down to the mouths of the little ones.

And there was no bread in all the land, because the famine was very heavy, and the land of Egypt and the land of Canaan wasted away because of the famine. And Joseph gathered up all the silver to be found in the land of Egypt and in the land of Canaan, in exchange for the grain they were buying, and Joseph brought the silver into Pharaoh's house. And when the silver was gone from the land of Egypt and from the land of Canaan, all Egypt came to Joseph and said, “Give us bread. Why should we die in front of you? For the silver is gone.” And Joseph said, “Give your livestock, and I will give to you in exchange for your livestock, if the silver is gone.” And they brought their livestock to Joseph, and Joseph gave them bread in exchange for the horses, and for the flocks of sheep, and for the herds of cattle, and for the donkeys. He carried them through that year with bread, in exchange for all their livestock. And that year ended, and they came to him the second year and said to him, “We cannot hide from my lord that the silver is gone, and the herds of animals are my lord's. Nothing is left before my lord but our bodies and our land. Why should we die before your eyes, both we and our land? Buy us and our land for bread, and we with our land will be slaves to Pharaoh. And give us seed, so that we live and do not die, and the land does not turn to waste.”

So Joseph bought all the land of Egypt for Pharaoh, because the Egyptians each sold his field, because the famine was too strong for them; and the land became Pharaoh's. And as for the people, he moved them into the cities, from one end of Egypt's border to the other. Only the land of the priests he did not buy, because the priests had a fixed allowance from Pharaoh, and they ate from the allowance Pharaoh gave them. That is why they did not sell their land. And Joseph said to the people, “Look, today I have bought you and your land for Pharaoh. Here is seed for you; sow the land. And at the harvests you are to give a fifth to Pharaoh, and four parts will be yours — as seed for the field, and as food for yourselves and for those in your households, and as food for your little ones.” And they said, “You have saved our lives. Let us find favor in the eyes of my lord, and we will be Pharaoh's slaves.” And Joseph made it a law over the land of Egypt, to this day: a fifth belongs to Pharaoh. Only the land of the priests did not become Pharaoh's.

And Israel settled in the land of Egypt, in the land of Goshen, and they took holdings in it, and were fruitful and multiplied greatly. And Jacob lived in the land of Egypt seventeen years, and the days of Jacob, the years of his life, were a hundred and forty-seven years. And the time drew near for Israel to die, and he called his son Joseph and said to him, “If I have found favor in your eyes, put your hand under my thigh, and deal with me in kindness and faithfulness: please do not bury me in Egypt. When I lie down with my fathers, carry me out of Egypt and bury me in their burial place.” And he said, “I will do as you say.” And he said, “Swear to me.” And he swore to him. And Israel bowed at the head of the bed.

chapters.label: Chapter 48
chapters.title: The Crossed Hands
paragraphs: And after these things Joseph was told, “Look, your father is ill.” And he took his two sons with him, Manasseh and Ephraim. And Jacob was told, “Look, your son Joseph has come to you.” And Israel gathered his strength and sat up on the bed. And Jacob said to Joseph, “El Shaddai appeared to me at Luz, in the land of Canaan, and blessed me, and said to me, ‘I am going to make you fruitful and multiply you, and I will make you a company of peoples, and I will give this land to your offspring after you as an everlasting holding.’ And now your two sons, who were born to you in the land of Egypt before I came to you in Egypt — they are mine. Ephraim and Manasseh will be mine, as Reuben and Simeon are. But the children you father after them will be yours; they will be called by their brothers' names in their inheritance. As for me, when I was coming from Paddan, Rachel died on me in the land of Canaan, on the road, when there was still some distance to go to Ephrath. And I buried her there on the road to Ephrath — that is, Bethlehem.”

And Israel saw Joseph's sons and said, “Who are these?” And Joseph said to his father, “They are my sons, whom God has given me here.” And he said, “Bring them to me, please, so I may bless them.” Now Israel's eyes were heavy with age; he could not see. And he brought them close to him, and he kissed them and embraced them. And Israel said to Joseph, “I never thought to see your face — and look, God has let me see your offspring too.” And Joseph took them from between his knees and bowed with his face to the ground. And Joseph took the two of them, Ephraim in his right hand, to Israel's left, and Manasseh in his left hand, to Israel's right, and brought them close to him. And Israel stretched out his right hand and laid it on Ephraim's head — and he was the younger — and his left hand on Manasseh's head. He crossed his hands, for Manasseh was the firstborn. And he blessed Joseph and said, “The God before whom my fathers Abraham and Isaac walked, the God who has been my shepherd all my life to this day, the messenger who has redeemed me from all harm — may he bless the boys. And may my name be called on them, and the name of my fathers Abraham and Isaac, and may they swarm into a multitude in the middle of the earth.”

And Joseph saw that his father had laid his right hand on Ephraim's head, and it was wrong in his eyes. And he took hold of his father's hand to move it from Ephraim's head to Manasseh's head. And Joseph said to his father, “Not so, my father. This one is the firstborn. Put your right hand on his head.” And his father refused and said, “I know, my son, I know. He too will become a people, and he too will be great. But his younger brother will be greater than he, and his offspring will become a fullness of nations.” And he blessed them that day, saying, “By you Israel will bless, saying, ‘May God make you like Ephraim and like Manasseh.’” And he put Ephraim before Manasseh. And Israel said to Joseph, “Look, I am about to die. But God will be with you, and will bring you back to the land of your fathers. And I give you one shoulder of land more than your brothers, which I took from the hand of the Amorites with my sword and my bow.”

chapters.label: Chapter 49
chapters.title: Jacob Blesses His Sons
paragraphs: And Jacob called his sons and said, “Gather, and I will tell you what will happen to you in the days to come. Come together and listen, sons of Jacob; listen to Israel your father.

“Reuben, you are my firstborn, my strength and the first fruit of my vigor, first in rank and first in power. Unstable as water, you will not be first — for you went up to your father's bed. Then you defiled it. My couch he went up to!

“Simeon and Levi are brothers; their weapons are tools of violence. Let my soul not enter their council; let my honor not be joined to their assembly. For in their anger they killed men, and at their pleasure they hamstrung oxen. Cursed be their anger, for it is fierce, and their fury, for it is cruel. I will divide them in Jacob, and scatter them in Israel.

“Judah — you, your brothers will praise. Your hand will be on the neck of your enemies; your father's sons will bow down to you. A lion's cub is Judah; from the prey, my son, you have gone up. He crouches, he lies down like a lion, like a lioness — who will rouse him? The scepter will not depart from Judah, nor the ruler's staff from between his feet, until Shiloh comes; and the obedience of peoples is his. He ties his donkey to the vine, his donkey's colt to the choice vine. He washes his clothes in wine, his robe in the blood of grapes. His eyes are darker than wine, and his teeth whiter than milk.
“Zebulun will live by the shore of the sea. He will be a shore for ships, and his flank will be at Sidon.

“Issachar is a strong-boned donkey, lying down between the saddlebags. He saw that rest was good, and that the land was pleasant, and he bent his shoulder to the load and became a slave at forced labor.

“Dan will judge his people as one of the tribes of Israel. Let Dan be a snake on the road, a viper on the path, that bites the horse's heels so its rider falls backward. For your salvation I wait, LORD.
“Gad — raiders will raid him, but he will raid at their heels.
“From Asher, his bread is rich, and he will provide the delicacies of a king.
“Naphtali is a doe let loose, who gives lovely words.

“Joseph is a fruitful bough, a fruitful bough by a spring, whose branches climb over the wall. The archers harassed him bitterly; they shot at him and bore him a grudge. But his bow stayed firm, and the arms of his hands were quick — by the hands of the Mighty One of Jacob, from there, the Shepherd, the Stone of Israel; by the God of your father, who will help you, and Shaddai, who will bless you with blessings of the sky above, blessings of the deep that lies below, blessings of the breasts and of the womb. The blessings of your father are mightier than the blessings of my ancestors, up to the bounds of the everlasting hills. May they be on the head of Joseph, on the brow of the one set apart from his brothers.
“Benjamin is a wolf that tears. In the morning he eats the prey, and in the evening he divides the spoil.”

All these are the tribes of Israel, twelve, and this is what their father said to them. He blessed them, each with the blessing that was his. And he commanded them and said to them, “I am about to be gathered to my people. Bury me with my fathers, in the cave that is in the field of Ephron the Hittite, in the cave in the field of Machpelah, which faces Mamre, in the land of Canaan — the field Abraham bought from Ephron the Hittite as a burial holding. There they buried Abraham and Sarah his wife. There they buried Isaac and Rebekah his wife. And there I buried Leah. The field and the cave in it were bought from the Hittites.” And when Jacob finished commanding his sons, he drew his feet up into the bed, and he breathed his last and was gathered to his people.

chapters.label: Chapter 50
chapters.title: God Meant It for Good
paragraphs: And Joseph fell on his father's face and wept over him and kissed him. And Joseph commanded his servants the physicians to embalm his father, and the physicians embalmed Israel. Forty days were taken for him, for that is how long the embalming takes; and the Egyptians wept for him seventy days. And when the days of weeping for him were past, Joseph spoke to Pharaoh's household: “If I have found favor in your eyes, please speak in Pharaoh's ears and say, ‘My father made me swear, saying: Look, I am about to die. In my grave that I dug for myself in the land of Canaan — there you are to bury me. So now let me go up, please, and bury my father, and I will come back.’” And Pharaoh said, “Go up and bury your father, as he made you swear.”

And Joseph went up to bury his father, and with him went up all Pharaoh's servants, the elders of his house and all the elders of the land of Egypt, and all Joseph's household, and his brothers, and his father's household. Only their little ones and their flocks and their herds they left in the land of Goshen. And chariots and horsemen went up with him too, and the camp was very large. And they came to the threshing floor of Atad, which is beyond the Jordan, and there they mourned with a very great and heavy mourning, and he kept seven days of mourning for his father. And the people of the land, the Canaanites, saw the mourning at the threshing floor of Atad and said, “This is a heavy mourning for Egypt.” That is why it was named Abel-mizraim, which is beyond the Jordan. And his sons did for him just as he had commanded them. His sons carried him to the land of Canaan and buried him in the cave of the field of Machpelah, the field facing Mamre that Abraham had bought as a burial holding from Ephron the Hittite. And Joseph went back to Egypt, he and his brothers and all who had gone up with him to bury his father, after he had buried his father.

And Joseph's brothers saw that their father was dead, and they said, “What if Joseph bears a grudge against us, and pays us back in full for all the evil we did him?” And they sent word to Joseph: “Your father gave this command before he died: ‘Say this to Joseph: Please, forgive the offense of your brothers and their sin, for they did you evil.’ So now, please forgive the offense of the servants of the God of your father.” And Joseph wept when they spoke to him. And his brothers also came and fell down before him and said, “Here we are, your slaves.” And Joseph said to them, “Do not be afraid. Am I in God's place? You planned evil against me; God planned it for good, to do what is being done today — to keep many people alive. So now, do not be afraid. I will provide for you and your little ones.” And he comforted them and spoke to their hearts.

And Joseph lived in Egypt, he and his father's household, and Joseph lived a hundred and ten years. And Joseph saw the third generation of Ephraim's children; the children of Machir son of Manasseh were also born on Joseph's knees. And Joseph said to his brothers, “I am about to die. But God will surely come to you and bring you up from this land to the land he swore to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob.” And Joseph made the sons of Israel swear: “God will surely come to you, and you are to carry my bones up from here.” And Joseph died, a hundred and ten years old. And they embalmed him, and he was laid in a coffin in Egypt.
